about.title: Rolling Hills Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Rolling Hills is a small place. With roughly 1,893 residents, a loss here is felt by neighbors, not just relatives. Public records for 2025 show a single injury collision in the city and no traffic deaths, which means fatal crashes are uncommon on roads like Crenshaw Boulevard, Crest Road West, Pathfinder Road and the 900 block of Silver Spur Road. Wrongful death claims, though, are not limited to traffic. A fall on poorly kept property, a medical error, a defective product, or a collision elsewhere in Los Angeles County can each give rise to a civil claim. California law lets a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children bring that claim first, with certain dependents and heirs able to step in when they are absent. Most families have two years from the date of death to file, and less time if a public agency is involved. The claim is separate from any criminal case, and it can cover funeral costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. LawProactive helps Rolling Hills families find an attorney who will handle this gently.

whyChoose.title: How LawProactive Helps Rolling Hills Families

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: Awareness of the two-year deadline
items.desc: The clock generally runs two years from the date of death, and a claim against a city, county or state agency must be started much sooner. Connecting early keeps those dates from slipping.

items.title: Recovery that reflects the whole loss
items.desc: Wrongful death damages in California include funeral and burial expenses, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Rolling Hills had no traffic deaths in 2025. Can my family still have a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: Yes. The public-record count for city streets like Crest Road West or Pathfinder Road only reflects collisions inside Rolling Hills. A wrongful death claim can arise from a crash anywhere in Los Angeles County, or from causes that have nothing to do with driving, such as medical negligence, an unsafe property, or a defective product. What matters is whether another party's carelessness caused the death.

items.question: The person responsible is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death case is a civil action and runs on its own track, separate from the district attorney's case. You do not need a conviction to bring a claim, and a criminal acquittal does not end your right to pursue one. An attorney can explain how the two may affect each other in your situation.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge our family anything?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm; we simply connect you with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death matters. The attorneys in our network work on a contingency basis, meaning they are paid only if there is a recovery. Your first conversation is about understanding your options, not about a bill.
